title.narrative: Promoting Socio-Economic Resilience & Social Cohesion in Niassa (JP-UNH-IOM)
Promoting Socio-Economic Resilience & Social Cohesion in Niassa (JP-UNH-IOM)

description.narrative:
The United Nations Human Settlement Programme (UN Habitat) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM) have submitted a three-year joint project document entitled "Nexus Niassa: Promoting socio-economic resilience and social cohesion in Niassa province through an integrated approach to development and peacebuilding".
Purpose and target group
The aim is to increase the resilience and stability of communities through inclusive development and improved living conditions in Niassa. To achieve the overall purpose, the project will focus on three result areas;
Strengthening the resilience of four identified communities, through conflict management and work to strengthen community cohesion and build positive social relations, with a particular focus on women and young people who are at risk or directly affected by the conflict in the neighbouring province of Cabo Delgado. Strengthening the state's presence at district and provincial level, through strengthening community services, administration, accountability, and civil society participation.
Empowering communities, especially women and children at risk or directly affected by through capacity development in financial inclusion and livelihoods, as well as improved living conditions and stability.
The project will apply an integrated and flexible approach and work with local authorities, communities and individuals, where UNHabitat will support state institutions with territorial planning and development, and IOM will work community empowering and stabilizing and implement interventions tailored to each community where the project is active. The project has a total budget of SEK 78 million.
The target group for the project is decision-makers and staff in public administration at all levels, districts, provinces and indirectly also state, local leaders and administrative associations in the communities where the project operates, civil society organizations, as well as residents of the identified communities with a focus (though not exclusively) on women and young people (both young women and men) as well as internally displaced people.
The project counts that direct beneficiaries will be: -236 457 inhabitants of the 4 target districts (77.808 in Marrupa, 68.260 in Maua, 45.303 in Metarica and 45.086 in Nipepe) with improved access to participatory governance and service provision (with priority on education and health). -20,000 people with access to birth certificates and ID cards (of which 12,000 women and 8,000 men, comprised of 10,000 youth). -6000 people (with at least 50% women) with increased security of tenure at settlement level 300 participants supported in capacity development on planning for resilience and engaged in participatory planning processes. -200 participants trained and capacitated in building activities on resilient construction. -600 people, between men and women, directly benefitting from income generation packages. 160 members of peace clubs trained in eight communities (20 in each).

United Nations Human Settlement Programme (UN Habitat) och International Organization for Migration (IOM) har inkommit med ett treårigt gemensamt projektdokument med titeln "Nexus Niassa: Främja socioekonomisk motståndskraft och social sammanhållning i Niassaprovinsen genom en integrerad strategi för utveckling och fredsbyggande”.
Syfte och målgrupp
Syftet är att öka samhällens motståndskraft och stabilitet genom inkluderande utveckling och förbättrade levnadsvillkor i Niassa. För att uppnå det övergripande syftet kommer projektet att fokusera på tre resultatområden;
Stärkande av fyra identifierade samhällens resiliens, genom konflikthantering och arbete för att stärka samhörighet i samhällena samt bygga positiva sociala relationer med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och ungdomar som är i riskzon eller direkt påverkade av konflikten i grannprovinsen Cabo Delgado. Stärkande av statens närvaro på distrikts och provinsnivå, genom stärkande av samhällstjänster, förvaltning, ansvarsutkrävande, och deltagande från civilsamhället.
Stärka samhällen, speciellt kvinnor och barn i riskzon eller direkt påverkade av konflikten, genom kapacitetsutveckling inom finansiell inkludering och försörjningsmöjligheter samt förbättrade levnadsvillkor och stabilitet.
Projektet kommer att tillämpa ett integrerat och flexibelt tillvägagångssätt och arbeta med lokala myndigheter, samhällen och individer, där UNHabitat kommer att stödja statliga institutioner med territoriell planering och utveckling, och IOM kommer att arbeta samhällsstärkande och stabiliserande och genomföra insatser som är skräddarsydda för varje samhälle där projektet är aktivt. Projektet har en total budget på 78 MSEK.
Målgruppen för projektet är beslutsfattare och personal inom offentlig förvaltning på alla nivåer, distrikt provins och indirekt även statlig, lokala ledare och administrativa föreningar i de samhällena där projektet är verksamt, civilsamhällsorganisationer, samt invånare i de identifierade samhällena med ett fokus (dock ej exkluderande) på kvinnor och ungdomar (både unga kvinnor och män) samt internflyktingar.
Projektet beräknar att nå: -236 457 individer i de fyra distrikt som projektet är Verksamt 77 808 i Marrupa, 68 260 i Maua, 45 303 i Metarica och 45 086 i Nipepe och förbättra deras delaktighet i offentlig förvaltning och tillgång till samhällstjänster (med fokus på hälsa och utbildning). -Vidare beräknas 20 000 männsikor få tillgång till födelsebevis och ID kort, 6000 individer varav minst 50% kvinnor med stärkta markrättigheter för bosättning, 300 personer stöds med kapacitetsutveckling för samhällsplanering med fokus på resiliens, 200 personer kommer tränas inom resilient byggande, 600 personer kommer ta del av inkomstgenererande aktiviteter och 160 medlemmar i fredsklubbarna från åtta samhällen kommer att ta del av kapacitetsutveckling inom fredsbyggande.

The project has an overarching goal of promoting socio-economic resilience and social cohesion in Niassa Province through an integrated development and peace-building approach. The main objective, as set out as the project's objective is "to enhance community resilience and stability through inclusive development and improved living conditions in Niassa Province". The main objective remains unchanged in the phase out amendment.
This objective is underpinned by three main outcomes;
1) The resilience of communities, especially women and youth at risk of or affected by conflict, is strengthened through the promotion of social cohesion and conflict resolution mechanisms.
2) The Government presence and capacities at provincial and local levels are increased, strengthening service delivery, governance, accountability and citizen participation.
3) Communities, especially women and youth at risk of or affected by conflict, are empowered through economic inclusion and livelihood opportunities and the promotion of improved living conditions and stability.
Primarily two districts in the south western parts of Niassa have been chosen for the intervention; Marrupa and Nipepe.
The revised approach respects the intended outcomes and does not challenge the original theory of change. The revised workplan will focus on four revised key areas:
Territorial Structuring through Land Readjustment: As a foundational intervention supporting the programmes territorial development approach, the land-related component will be implemented through a structured and readjustment process combining spatial analysis, participatory planning and institutional coordination with district authorities. The intervention will focus on two priority neighbourhoods identified through the City Resilience Action Planning (CityRAP) process as areas with high exposure to climaterelated risks and significant spatial disorganization. The land readjustment process aims to improve spatial organization and strengthen tenure management while creating the structural conditions required for improved service provision and future infrastructure investments. By reorganizing plots and defining public spaces and service corridors, the intervention will contribute to a more resilient and functional urban structure within the targeted communities.
Institutional Strengthening of District Technical Services: A key element of the implementation strategy is the strong institutional involvement of both district and provincial authorities in the delivery of the land readjustment intervention. To formalize this collaboration, UN-Habitat will establish two complementary Letters of Agreement: one with the district administrations through the Serviço Distrital de Planeamento e Infraestruturas (SDPI), and another with the Provincial Directorate of Land and Environment (DPTMA). Throughout the process, both institutions will receive continuous technical guidance and methodological support from UN-Habitat specialists, ensuring that the intervention is implemented in accordance with national land management frameworks while strengthening the technical capacity of local administrations. This implementation modality strengthens institutional ownership, promotes practical capacity building, and ensures that the technical methodologies introduced through the project remain embedded within district administrations beyond the project lifecycle.
Targeted Public Infrastructure and Service Improvements: In line with the revised implementation timeline, the programme consolidates its physical infrastructure interventions around a targeted set of strategic investments designed to improve connectivity, strengthen access to basic services, and reinforce the resilience of local communities. The implementation of these works will be carried out through an Agreement of Cooperation (AoC) with the Agência Nacional de Estradas (ANE), which will lead the procurement and execution of the infrastructure rehabilitation activities. This approach ensures technical compliance with national infrastructure standards while enabling the programme to leverage the operational capacity and technical expertise of the national road authority.
Community-Level Revitalization and Participatory Interventions: Complementing the programmes territorial restructuring and infrastructure investments, the project also supports community-level revitalization initiatives grounded in participatory planning processes. These interventions aim to ensure that local communities actively contribute to identifying priorities for improving their living environments and strengthening local resilience. Building on the results of the City Resilience Action Planning (CityRAP) process and the Matrix of Functions (MoF) exercises conducted with district authorities, the programme facilitated a series of Community-Based Planning (CBP) sessions within the targeted neighbourhoods. Through these consultations, communities identified a set of priority revitalization initiatives aimed at addressing key service gaps and improving local living conditions. The implementation of these interventions will be carried out in close coordination with district authorities and community representatives, ensuring that the selected initiatives remain technically feasible, socially accepted and aligned with the broader territorial planning processes supported by the programme. IOM will also ensure that the programme preserve community-based mechanisms that directly foster social cohesion, commutation with selected institutions to mitigate loss of trust from reduced activities, protection of livelihood and economic inclusion outcomes with immediate household-level impact, and lastly a focus on participatory and community-led revitalization processes with visible outcomes.

description.narrative:
See revised plan and progress report below:
EA1 - The resilience of communities, especially of women and youth at risk of or affected by conflict, is strengthened through the promotion of social cohesion and conflict resolution mechanisms.
Expected completion: 98% • Indicator: # of community members participating in peace clubs (disaggregated by gender and age) o Original Target: 160 participants o Modified Target: 100 participants o Justification: This number of the indicator directly reflects the community members participating in the peace clubs implemented by IOM.
Output 1.1 - Assessment on conflict sensitivity and social cohesion, including ongoing, flexible, adaptive research is conducted and validated. Expected completion: 100%
• Indicator 1: # of studies delivered on violent extremism in Mozambique o Original Target: 1 study o Modified Target: 1 study o Justification: Considering the complexity of conducting the conflict and violent extremism assessment, the revised project timeline allows for the delivery of a single comprehensive study covering the entire Province, instead of four separate reports as originally stipulated in the ProDoc.
• Indicator 2: # of workshops held to discuss research findings o Original Target: 1 workshop o Modified Target: 1 workshop o Justification: This workshop is expected to be completed by the end of the project period, allowing the original target to be fully maintained.
Output 1.2 - Sub-provincial functional analysis of Niassa Province and of the development triangle between Cuamba, Lichinga and Marrupa elaborated by the provincial and district governments to support strategic decision making. Expected completion: 133%
• Indicator: # of technicians trained in data collection and interpretation participating in planning activities linked with SDF/MoF tool in the prioritized districts and at provincial level o Original Target: 75 participants o Modified Target: 100 participants o Justification: This activity will be completed by the revised project deadline, with an expanded scope to ensure that all technicians originally planned to be trained are fully covered. The increase in the target reflects the expansion of the scope, which allows for the inclusion of a broader range of technical profiles.
Output 1.3 - Youth and women community-based peace clubs have capacities to promote conflict resolution and social cohesion. Expected completion: 63%
• Indicator: # of community members participating in peace clubs (at least 50% female, comprised of 30% youth) (disaggregated by gender and age) o Original Target: 160 participants o Modified Target: 100 participants o Justification: Only 100 of the originally planned Community-Based Planning (CBP) processes will be implemented due to the revised project scope; however, the adjusted target will be fully achieved.
Output 1.4 - Communities have access to improved community conflict mediation and reconciliation mechanisms. Expected completion: 133%
• Indicator 1: # of civic education campaigns implemented. o Original Target: 4 campaigns o Modified Target: 8 campaigns
• Indicator 2: % of training participants with increased knowledge on conflict resolution and mediation mechanisms
• Indicator 3: # of positive engagement trainings conducted o Original Target: 12 sessions o Modified Target: 8 sessions
• Indicator 4: % of participants of positive engagement trainings who improved the resilience after the training Justification: Each community targtted by the project will have two civic education campaings implemented within the revised timeline.
EA 2 - The Government capacities and presence at provincial and local levels are increased, strengthening governance, accountability and citizen participation, as well as contributing to more equitable service provision and better territorial planning. Expected completion: 85%
• Indicator: # of people (disaggregated by sex and age) participating in participatory planning and management activities in the 4 prioritized districts o Original Target: 400 participants o Modified Target: 400 participants o Justification: All participatory planning activities will be completed in line with the revised project deadline, ensuring that the target is fully achieved. The estimate is calculated assuming an average of 100 participants per district.
Output 2.1 - Resilient Framework for Action (RFAs) elaborated by the Districts of Marrupa, Metarica, Nipepe and Maua through inclusive participatory processes and implemented at district level through leveraged funding of different initiatives. Expected completion: 100%
• Indicator 1: # of Resilient Frameworks for Action formulated, approved by district governments and supporting the actualization/formulation of the Local Adaptation Plans (LAPs) of the target districts o Original Target: 4 studies o Modified Target: 4 studies o Justification: All RFA-related activities are already underway and will be completed within the revised project deadline, allowing the original target to be fully achieved.
• Indicator 2: # of participants to participatory workshops with local stakeholders and communities. o Original Target: 200 participants o Modified Target: 200 participants o Justification: With the completion of the RFAs, the targeted number of participants in participatory workshops will be achieved, ensuring inclusive engagement of local stakeholders and communities.
Output 2.2 - Investing in civil Society and community-based organizations improved local participatory and inclusive governance and strengthen social Cohesion. Expected completion: 0%
• Indicator 1: # of civil society organizations capacitated. o Original Target: 4 CSOs o Modified Target: 0 CSOs • Indicator 2: % of participating civil society members feel increased organizational capacity. Justification: This output relies on the engagement of civil society organizations (CSOs) and requires a lot of capacity building and very close supervision. In light of the revised project timeline, the processes required to identify, contract, and administer grants to CSO are no longer feasible, and therefore the small grants component will not be implemented.
Output 2.3 - District Resilient Public Facilities Improvement Packages implemented in the districts of Marrupa, Metarica, Nipepe and Maua, for improved service provision and quality of life. Expected completion: 148% • Indicator 1: # of public infrastructure rehabilitated, reconstructed or built under the scope of the project o Original Target: 12 Public Infrastructures o Modified Target: 04 Public Infrastructures Justification: The revised target is based on the number of priority construction elements required to restore critical connectivity along the R723 road corridor. In total, 23 intervention sites are planned, including the rehabilitation of 2 bridges, 5 aqueducts, and 16 earthwork interventions to address the most urgent structural constraints affecting mobility and access. In addition, two Sede de Bairro facilities will be constructed in the same neighborhoods where land readjustment activities will be implemented, ensuring that the infrastructure investments directly support the territorial planning process and improve local governance and service access within the targeted communities.
• Indicator 2: # of people, disaggregated by gender and age, to have restored access to specific public services (depending on the final typology included in the district portfolios) o Original Target: 120.000 people o Modified Target: 172.323 people o Justification: According to information provided by provincial and district authorities, this intervention is expected to rebalance the development dynamics within the Niassa regional corridor while generating direct benefits for the populations of Nipepe and Marrupa districts. The rehabilitation of the R723 road will significantly improve connectivity by providing Nipepe with a shorter and more reliable route to Montepuez and Pemba, while Marrupa will gain improved access to Nampula and the Nacala Corridor, strengthening regional economic integration and access to markets and services. For this reason, the revised beneficiary target considers the combined population of Nipepe and Marrupa. The communities located along the R723 corridor include Muacuaciua, Massaca, Napalavi, Arama, Morrico, Cumbira, and Malia, all within the Nipepe Sede Administrative Post, while the community directly affected by the intervention is Maiaia, located in the Nungo Administrative Post.
• Indicator 3: # of civil servants (teachers, health, public function and other staff) working in a resilient and safe infrastructure. o Original Target: 720 civil servants o Modified Target: 1000 civil servants o Justification: This figure represents the estimated number of civil servants expected to benefit from the interventions related to the R723 road rehabilitation and the construction of the two Sede de Bairro facilities. The estimate remains preliminary and will need to be confirmed through coordination with the district authorities, as it requires cross-checking the number of personnel currently working across the diVerent district services in Marrupa and Nipepe.
• Indicator 4: # of participants in training and capacity building activities on resilient construction (disaggregated by institution, sex and age); o Original Target: 200 participants o Modified Target: 200 civil servants o Justification: Each Sede de Bairro construction will serve as an on-the-job training opportunity, allowing UN-Habitat to implement the resilient construction training package previously developed. It is estimated that approximately 100 local artisans and government technicians will be involved in the training for each construction, strengthening local technical capacities in resilient building practices while supporting the implementation of the infrastructure works.
Output 2.4 - Increase the capacity of government to provide women and men in the communities with access to civil documentation. Expected completion: 75% • Indicator 1: # of birth certificates and ID cards delivered (60% women and 40% men, comprised of 50% youth) o Original Target: 20.000 documents facilitated o Modified Target: 15.000 documents facilitated Justification: Due to the shortened timeline for implementation, the target has been reduced to 15,000.
EA 3 - Communities, especially women - youth at risk of or aVected by conflict, are empowered through economic inclusion and livelihood opportunities and the promotion of community resilience, stability and increased living conditions. Expected completion: 69%
• Indicator 1: # of hectares of neighborhood land readjusted and with increased formalization in tenure and managed according to the existing rules and regulations o Original Target: 24 hectares o Modified Target: 12 hectares o Justification: As a core activity underpinning all subsequent construction and physical interventions, the scope of this intervention has been expanded to include urban expansion alongside land readjustment. Nevertheless, due to the revised project timeline, implementation will be confined to two districts, covering an estimated total area of 12 hectares.
• Indicator 2: # people in communities benefitting from infrastructure improvements. (Disaggregated by institution, sex and age) o Original Target: 6000 people o Modified Target: 6000 people o Justification: This target corresponds to the population of the neighborhoods targeted under the land readjustment component. It is expected that these beneficiaries will also be counted under the Outcome indicator, as they will benefit from both the land readjustment activities and the associated infrastructure interventions.
Output 3.1 - Land Readjustment Intervention and Resilient housing promotion packages in one priority neighborhood at district capital level (vila sede) per each target district to boost participatory local development and increased resilience. Expected completion: 63%
• Indicator 1: # of households included in neighborhoods with increased formalization and readjustment of land with related management instruments. o Original Target: 1.200 households o Modified Target: 600 households o Justification: Given that land readjustment will be implemented in only two communities, the target for this indicator will be reduced by 50%. These communities are in the districts of Marrupa (Cafezeiros) and Nipepe (Rehereque).
• Indicator 2: # Number of people, disaggregated by gender and age, to have improved knowledge on resilient housing solutions. o Original Target: 6.000 people o Modified Target: 6.000 people o Justification: This indicator represents the total population of the two neighborhoods targeted under the land readjustment component.
• Indicator 3: # of resilient pilot housing units built for vulnerable households. o Original Target: 20 house units o Modified Target: 0 house units o Justification: No housing construction will be implemented under this programme. The budget initially allocated for this component has been reallocated to support the public infrastructure interventions under Output 2.3.
• Indicator 4: # of participants in training and capacity building activities on resilient construction (disaggregated by institution, sex and age). o Original Target: 200 participants o Modified Target: 200 participants o Justification: This indicator reflects the same group of beneficiaries counted under Output 2.3, as they will participate in two cycles of training. The first cycle will focus on resilient construction techniques, while the second will address community infrastructure maintenance, ensuring that community focal points and local artisans are properly equipped with the skills required to maintain and repair the infrastructure delivered by IOM.
Output 3.2 - Resilient Community Infrastructure Improvement Packages per each target district, implemented with the engagement of communities (in particular youth and women) and consultative processes, to prioritize and implement community revitalization projects for social benefit. Expected completion: 100%
• Indicator 1: # community-based planning sessions conducted. o Original Target: 4 sessions o Modified Target: 4 sessions o Justification: All four community-based planning activities will be conducted in accordance with the originally defined deadline, with implementation concentrated in two districts. • Indicator 2: # of community revitalization initiatives implemented; o Original Target: 8 initiatives o Modified Target: 8 initiatives o Justification: This target will be fully achieved, with implementation concentrated in two districts and aligned with the same communities where the Community- Based Planning (CBP) processes are being implemented.
• Indicator 3: % of CBP participants with perceived increase of harmony in the community.
Output 3.3 - Community-driven income generation and livelihood opportunities for community members, particularly women and youth with vulnerabilities. Expected completion: 33%
• Indicator 1: # of people benefitting from income generation support. o Original Target: 3.000 people o Modified Target: 1.000 people o Justification: This indicator represents the number of individuals benefiting from the delivery of income-generation packages. For each package provided to a household, it is estimated that five members of the same family will directly benefit.
• Indicator 2: # of income generation packages distributed (at least 50% to women, comprised of 30% youth). o Original Target: 600 packages o Modified Target: 200 packages o Justification: Due to the reduced project timeline, IOM will only be able to deliver half of the planned income-generation packages; consequently, 200 of the originally planned 600 packages will be delivered.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
